Hi Priyom,

Thanks for picking this up. As part of our procurement and clinical data governance review we need a concise DPF/locality assurance package and a DPA Annex we can circulate to our legal and infosec teams. Specific asks from our side:

- A DPF evidence pack (operational controls, routing options, retention and logging) that explains how requests are routed by region and what controls exist to prevent egress to non-US jurisdictions.

We need this by COB Wednesday if possible so our legal/compliance review can start. I attached our procurement questionnaire to speed things up. If it's easier to schedule a 30-min call, please propose times.

Thanks, Rishi and Priyom. A couple of clarifying questions from security:

1) KMS: Do you support a BYOK model where the key material never leaves our KMS (we'd like explicit language to that effect for the DPA annex if supported)?
2) Model routing / execution: PharmaLine's requirement is that all processing of PHI for our tenant must remain in US-only physical infrastructure unless we explicitly approve otherwise. Can Redwood provide a contractual routing guarantee (i.e., region pin + contractual obligation) or is that only available with Private/Dedicated?
3) Can you provide a simple keyflow diagram and the specific logging fields we can ingest into our SIEM?

I've attached our internal compliance checklist to show the fields we'll map. We'll review your redline but please flag anything you think will require an internal legal escalation.

Regards,

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@pharmaline.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial RFP Qs: cross-border routing / DPA annex / DPF evidence

Hi Sarah — looping in technical detail. Short answers up front, then specifics below.

- BYOK: yes, we support true BYOK where key material is managed in your KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can bind the key lifecycle to your tenant; the key material is never exported from your KMS. We'll propose DPA language to reflect that for the Dedicated/Private path.

- Residency / routing guarantees: Redwood Hosted offers routing policies (region preference, cost/latency tiers) but cannot unilaterally guarantee physical execution only in a single country across our shared hosted fleet. For a contractual residency guarantee you should select Redwood Dedicated with region pinning or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — both give you contractual control over execution location. We can, however, provide a contract-level routing commitment for Hosted that says "requests will be routed preferentially to US-only pools and any exception will trigger notification and fallback" — Rishi's redline includes this option.

- Keyflow and logging: attached is a diagram (kms_keyflow_diagram.png) and a logging field map (we've included a table in dpf_evidence_v3.pdf). Important fields you can ingest to SIEM: request_id, tenant_id, model_id, origin_ip, routed_region, cache_hit, kms_key_id (masked), token_usage_bytes, auth_subject. We stream audit logs to a configurable retention window and can offer syslog/forwarder delivery for Dedicated/Private.

- SOC2 & artifacts: we can provide SOC 2 Type II summary under NDA and a redacted control matrix now — see the evidence pack.

Links & attachments:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bREDWOOD-DPF-evidence
- Attachments: kms_keyflow_diagram.png; dpf_evidence_v3.pdf

If that aligns with your compliance needs, Priyom can scope Dedicated vs Private options and associated pricing. Happy to jump on the call Priyom suggested — I can take the technical portion.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager, Platform Security, Redwood Inference
Attachments: kms_keyflow_diagram.png; dpf_evidence_v3.pdf
